recipe: span return with inverse-noise loss weighting (Rw)
recipe_description: the copy-pointer carrier network (61,613 parameters) trained from scratch per population on a pooled training set (windows whose labels end before the population's validation set), early stopping on the population's last 93 days before the training cut (at most 30 epochs, patience 5); then the 93-day validation span returned to the training set at the population's own sampling density (labels ending within 24 h of the cut not returned) and training continued from the selected weights with a fresh AdamW for exactly 8 epochs, final weights kept; the loss of these 8 epochs weighted per training window by the frozen inverse-noise rule (omega = max(sigma^2, floor)^-1/2, sigma^2 from the window's own context day tokens 338..365 against the same hours 7 days earlier, floor = the draw-probability-weighted 25th percentile, weights normalised to a draw-weighted mean of 1 within each source population); seeds 0 to 5 averaged at every issue time, anchored by the unchanged ANKYRA 2.2.1 anchoring layer, weekly seasonal naive on off-state and micro-load windows; then the origin-continuity layer (ankyra_lite.continuation, frozen constants) on the anchored trajectory of the other windows, with energy, level and peak read before the layer (readout rule A)

format: torch.save of {'model': state_dict, 'epoch': 8} (the stage-2 run's final weights, copied byte for byte); ankyra_lite.load_carrier(path) loads it strictly on the CPU
use: one checkpoint per population and seed; pass the population's training cut as cut= and use origins at least 186 days after it; a forecast with all six seeds is the plain average of their forecasts at every issue time, summed in ascending seed order (ankyra_lite.checkpoint_paths returns them so); six seeds take about twice the carrier inference time of three
